candidates.summary: the cap note promises "the changed realms are always kept" while the cap drops them, and the comment still links the dropped ones
candidates.failure_scenario: A pull request that edits more realm directories than -max-realms (default 25) — an examples/ wide migration or a gno fmt sweep — reaches BuildPlan, which stable-sorts the changed realms first and then truncates the whole list at the cap (plan.go:256-259) with no floor for them. Measured with 3 changed realms and maxRealms 2: Realms=[gno.land/r/a gno.land/r/b], ChangedRealms=[gno.land/r/a gno.land/r/b gno.land/r/c], Dropped=1. Comment then lists all three under **Changed realms (3)** with links into the snapshot for r/c that was never rendered (page, _t/source/, _t/help/ — all 404 on Pages), and closes with the line at 86 telling the reviewer the changed realms were kept. The realm the PR is about is the one the reviewer cannot see, and the comment says the opposite.

candidates.evidence: --- FAIL: TestB5DroppedChangedRealmAgainstTheNote; "ChangedRealms=[gno.land/r/a gno.land/r/b gno.land/r/c] Realms=[gno.land/r/a gno.land/r/b] Dropped=1"; "changed realm \"gno.land/r/c\" was dropped by the cap, yet the comment links https://example.test/pr-1/r/c/"; comment body carries "- [`gno.land/r/c`](https://example.test/pr-1/r/c/) · [source](…) · [help](…)" above "⚠️ 1 more affected realm(s) were **not** rendered (cap reached) — the changed realms are always kept."

candidates.summary: realm package paths are written unescaped into the comment's HTML attributes and markdown links, and a privileged job posts that body verbatim
candidates.failure_scenario: The PR body's assurance about the untrusted comment body covers shell interpolation only ("passes it as a file and never interpolates it into a shell command. It cannot reach a secret"); the body is still markup a fork controls. Every realm string in it is a directory name from the fork's tree — BuildPlan derives gno.land/r/ straight from examples/gno.land/r/ with no validation (plan.go:136-141), measured: a directory named `evil)](https://attacker.example/)[x` becomes ChangedRealms[0]. comment.go writes that string raw into alt="%s" (112, 118, 121) and into [`%s`](…) (33). Measured output: `alt="x">"` — the attribute is closed and an attacker-hosted image is embedded in a comment pr-preview-publish.yml posts under the repository's own token; GitHub's comment sanitizer keeps img/src and a/href, so the result is a third-party beacon and arbitrary links inside what reads as a bot message.
candidates.verify_by: cp the artifact and run `go test ./... -run TestB5CommentEscapesRealmNames -v` in misc/gnopreview; then settle the remaining step end to end — boot gnodev on a package dir whose name carries `"` or `)` and see whether it serves, since the render job writes no comment.md if gnodev refuses to boot on plan.Dirs.

candidates.summary: the exported CommentMarker const is not what makes the comment sticky; pr-preview-publish.yml carries its own copy of the literal
candidates.failure_scenario: The godoc says the const is what the publishing job matches on. The job matches on its own hardcoded string instead (.github/workflows/pr-preview-publish.yml:169, marker='<!-- gnoweb-pr-preview -->'), and no test or build step ties the two. Editing the Go const alone still compiles and still passes plan_test.go (which asserts the body contains CommentMarker, whatever its value), and the next push to every open PR posts a second comment instead of updating the first — the failure the const exists to prevent, and it is invisible until a PR carries two previews.
